crime_highlights: Mr. Gairdner, then aged 34, and weighing some 300 pounds, violently attacked T.D.
he hit her in the eye, causing very serious injury to the eye area, as well as injuries to her neck and nose
Off camera, she was choked by him
She later had to have reconstructive surgery on her eye and had no vision in her left eye for about two months
rationale_highlights: In my view, they took into consideration all the relevant mitigating factors, including the fact of Mr. Gairdner's aboriginal antecedents.
These of course are many of the factors that characterize the lives of many of our indigenous people, and that Gladue seeks to have reflected in sentencing decisions under the Code.
I am not persuaded that a five-year sentence was unfit or that the court failed to give appropriate consideration to the appellant's aboriginal background
note: Appeal upheld five years; court says Gladue considered but never states a reduction.

crime_highlights: While before the courts on those offences, he committed the same offence between October 1, 2013, and January 5, 2014.
Mr. Isbister groomed the teenaged boys, who were each 14 years old at the time of the offences, by befriending them, giving them alcohol, drugs and cash.
He offended over a long period of time, for over a year with two of the children and for three months with the third.
Mr. Isbister has used alcohol and drugs as enticements to lure vulnerable teenagers into eventually obtaining sexual favours from them.
rationale_highlights: he failed to address the fact that Mr. Isbister is Métis, and take into account s. 718.2(e) and the Gladue factors
there is no requirement for a causal connection between Indigenous heritage and offending
That error and the failure to apply the Gladue principles, in my view, led the sentencing judge to impose an unfit sentence.
note: Crime passage describes original sexual offences, not the breach being sentenced.

crime_highlights: She woke up at 1:30 a.m. to find she was being held down in her bed with hard pressure applied to her chest and inner thigh.
Initially she was unable to move but eventually did so and realized the assailant was her cousin.
rationale_highlights: Like many Indigenous offenders who find themselves before the court, the appellant has been disproportionately affected by systemic discrimination, abuse, dislocation from culture or family and substance abuse.
The appellant was raised by his grandparents, both of whom attended residential schools

given the systemic issues to be addressed, the appellant's status as a first-time offender, the nature of the offence and the appellant's family circumstances, these factors must be taken into account to arrive at an appropriate sentence
the sentence imposed should not have been as harsh
note: Victim effects are in para 16 and 7, not adjacent to crime passage.
